strings: A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.

A flimsy model of a standard Nanotrasen automated mindshield implant machine. With secure positioning harnesses and a robotic surgical injector, brain damage and other serious medical anomalies are now up to 60% less likely!
A one meter section of regular pipe.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
Come get your own gold plaque!
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
A metal tray to lay food on.
It produces items using iron, glass, plastic and maybe some more.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with generic programs.
A desk lamp with an adjustable mount.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
A poster instructing the viewer to walk instead of running.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
It's coarse and rough and gets everywhere.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
A magnetic tape that can hold up to ten minutes of content on either side.
A device that can record to cassette tapes, and play them. It automatically translates the content in playback.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
It's a secure locker for personnel. The first person to swipe their ID gains control.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
The intergalactic symbol of medical institutions. You'll probably get help here.
Heats or cools gas in connected pipes.
A special pipe to bridge pipe layers with.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
Dispenses pipes that will ultimately be used to move trash around.
A head-mounted face cover designed to protect the wearer completely from space-arc eye.
A figurine depicting a Lawyer sporting a freshly tailored suit.
Has a valve and pump attached to it. There are two ports.
A console used for high-priority announcements and emergencies.

A highly precise directional sensor array which measures the release of quants from decaying tachyons. The doppler shifting of the mirror-image formed by these quants can reveal the size, location and temporal affects of energetic disturbances within a large radius ahead of the array.
It's a storage unit for emergency breath masks and O2 tanks.
A sign that warns of extremely hot air in the vicinity.
A human incinerator. Works well on barbecue nights.
A thin layer of dust coating the floor.
Ding-aling ding dong. Get your Nanotrasen-approved ice cream!
A basic, dull, white chef's apron.
The original knife, it is said that all other knives are only copies of this one.
The commander in chef's head wear.
Lead-lined shutters with a radiation hazard symbol. Whilst this won't stop you getting irradiated, especially by a supermatter crystal, it will stop radiation travelling as far.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
Extremely sturdy interior hull plating that separates you from the floor below.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A radio beacon used for bot navigation.
A machine used to store data and network statistics.
Spinward Sector Station SS-06 'Pubby' Class Outpost Commissioned 19/10/2556 Decommissioned 10/12/2560 'No Law But Ours'
A face-covering mask that can be connected to an air supply. Good for concealing your identity and with a filter slot to help remove those toxins.
It's a baseball hat in a tasteless yellow colour.
An underfloor disposal pipe with a sorting mechanism.
It's a storage unit for fire-fighting supplies.
Four metal legs with four framing rods for a table. You could easily pass through this.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
It's a normal black ink pen.
A poster encouraging you to work for your future.
An old, deactivated cyborg. Whilst once actively used to guard against intruders, it now simply intimidates them with its cold, steely gaze.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images. This one will refuse to auto-connect incoming calls.
Sturdy interior hull plating that separates you from the floor below.
All engineering related spawners go here
Some rods. Can be used for building or something.
A coil of insulated power cable.
The flag of the Terran Government, home of humanity.
Used to keep bodies in until someone fetches them. Includes a high-tech alert system.
It's a storage unit for rad-protective suits.
A warning sign which reads 'NO SMOKING'.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
Magnetic boots, often used during extravehicular activity to ensure the user remains safely attached to the vehicle.
A tank full of industrial welding fuel. Do not consume.
Spinward Sector Station SS-12 'Asteroid' Class Outpost Commissioned 13/10/2555 Decommissioned 19/06/2556 'A Meteoric Success'
Used to reclaim your items after you finish your sentence at the labor camp.
A canister for the storage of gas.
This rock is filled with pockets of breathable air.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A hand-held body scanner capable of distinguishing vital signs of the subject. Has a side button to scan for chemicals, and can be toggled to scan wounds.
A close-fitting sterile mask that can be connected to an air supply.
Don't jump on it, or do, I'm not your mom.
A reinforced version of the glass table.
The HT-451, a torque rotation-based, waste disposal unit for small matter. This one seems remarkably clean.
A manifold composed of regular pipes.
A covered turret that shoots at its enemies.
Tiny bits of colored paper thrown about for the janitor to enjoy!
These gloves are cheap knockoffs of the coveted ones - no way this can end badly.
A one meter section of heat-exchanging pipe.
A plushie depicting an adorable mothperson. It's a huggable bug!
A poster showing a commissary menu from the Mothic fleet flagship, the Va Lümla. It lists various consumable items alongside prices in ration tickets.
This informational poster uses Safety Moth™ to tell atmospheric technicians correct types of piping to be used. \"Pipes, not Pumps! Proper pipe placement prevents poor performance!\"
Order, order! No bombs in my courthouse.
A large structural assembly made out of metal; It requires a layer of iron before it can be considered a wall.
Tastes just like the chef's soup.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Command department is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Security department is.
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
Made by Space Amish using traditional space techniques, this heater/cooler is guaranteed not to set the station on fire. Warranty void if used in engines.
